full_judgment:
3. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree, plaintiff-appellant has preferred this appeal alleging that the impugned judgment and decree is bad in law as well as in facts. The learned Subordinate Judge failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the case and also failed to apply his judicial mind in the records and dismissed the suit by making out a third case. The finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff-appellant has got no title in the suit land is not based on fact and the evidences on the record. To that effect plaintiff-appellant has submitted the CSSA and RS Khatians of the suit land which stands in the name of the Railway Authority. These documentary evidences have been overlooked by the learned trial Court. The finding of the trial Court that the suit is barred by limitation is erroneous. The Trial Court travelled beyond its jurisdiction and the finding that the defendant-respondents are entitled to claim compensation is illegal and not supported by any evidence as illegal possessors cannot get compensation for the land possessed by them. The finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff-respondents are entitled to compensation is without any basis as the suit land has not been acquired in LA Case Nos. 62/1964-65 and 14/1965-66. 

 6. On behalf of the respondents, the learned Senior Counsel Mr TH Khan submitted that the present Title Suit No. 94 of 1993 filed by the appellant is hopelessly barred by limitation, since the appellant was all along aware of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 279 of 1970. To that effect he has drawn our attention to the findings made by the trial Court in issue No. 2 wherein the trial Court by referring the specific legal notice 'Exhibit Kha' received by the present plaintiff who on 10-6-1985 wrote a letter to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA). Dhaka intimating him of the aforesaid judgment and decree (Exhibit 'Dha'). Under such circumstances, the Learned Counsel submitted that the period of limitation under Article 95 of the Limitation Act to set aside a judgment and decree on the ground of fraud is three years from the date of knowledge. So, he submitted that knowledge of the appellant about the impugned judgment and decree accrued long ago i.e. prior to three years of the specified period. Accordingly, he submitted that without overcoming the point of limitation the appellant cannot get any relief. On that point, the learned Advocate Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, who also appears on behalf of the respondents, referred Section 3 of the Limitation Act which runs thus: 

 "Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 25 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred and application made, after the period of limitation prescribed therefore by the first schedule shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence." 

 He submitted that this section is mandatory and when a plaint of a suit is presented beyond the period of limitation it is the duty of the Court to check and verify the same and if it is found to be barred by limitation, it is obligatory on the part of the Court to dismiss the suit forthwith by invoking the power of section 3 of the Limitation Act. 

 7. In this appeal, the point for determination before us is the legality and illegality of the impugned judgment and decree, dated 30-11-1994, passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Second Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 136 of 1994. It is admitted that the respondents—Badaruddin Ahmed, Moslehuddin Ahmed and Feroza Begum—as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 279 of 1970 in the Court of the then learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, That suit was contested by the defendants and the same was dismissed on contest on 24-8-1971. Against that judgment and decree the present respondents filed First Appeal No. 68 of 1972 before this Court and the impugned judgment and decree was set aside and the suit was sent back on remand for fresh trial. After receiving the record by the trial Court, both the parties filed fresh power. Thereafter, on 24-9-1984 the suit has been decreed ex parte. The present appellant has filed this Title Suit No. 94 of 1993 (re-numbered as Title Suit No. 139 of 1994) long after three years and the same is hopelessly barred by limitation. So, the learned trial Court rightly dismissed the suit. In view of that we do not find any merit in this appeal.
